skill.name: go-rod-master
skill.description: Guide for building Go browser automation with Rod, including scraping, waits, network interception, screenshots, page pools, and stealth features.
skill.summary: Build Go browser automation with Rod for scraping, testing, and Chrome DevTools workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are scanner noise from Go import blocks, Markdown backticks, Go raw strings, and example URLs. Real concerns are explicit anti-bot evasion guidance, SOCKS proxy use, TLS-error bypass for MITM proxies, and request/response hijacking examples. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot evasion guidance is presented as a default production pattern.
remediation.suggestion: Limit stealth guidance to authorized testing, remove bypass language for Cloudflare and bot detection, and add permission requirements.

remediation.issue: Proxy and TLS-error bypass examples can conceal automation or weaken transport security.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict proxy and IgnoreCertErrors examples to owned test environments and explain the security impact clearly.

remediation.issue: Request hijacking examples modify headers and JavaScript responses.
remediation.suggestion: Use harmless test domains, avoid authorization header examples, and state that interception must target owned systems only.

remediation.issue: The source metadata labels the skill as safe despite dual-use automation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Update the source risk statement to reflect network, proxy, interception, and anti-bot evasion capabilities.

content.user_title: Build Browser Automation With Go Rod
content.value_statement: Dynamic websites are hard to test and scrape with simple HTTP clients. This skill gives Rod patterns for Go automation, waits, interception, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Explains Rod browser, page, and element lifecycle patterns.
Shows selector, timeout, auto-wait, and event waiting techniques.
Covers stealth page setup and bot detection test workflows.
Demonstrates request interception, header changes, and response body changes.
Documents screenshots, PDF export, downloads, and JavaScript evaluation.
Shows page pooling for concurrent scraping with isolated browser contexts.
limitations: Requires Chromium or a compatible browser on the target system.
Does not solve CAPTCHAs or guarantee access through strict bot defenses.
Can create legal and policy risk if used on sites without permission.
Examples need adaptation for production error handling and rate limits.

use_cases.title: Automate Dynamic Web Pages
use_cases.description: Create Go workflows that navigate, wait for content, and extract rendered page data.

use_cases.title: Test Browser Interactions
use_cases.description: Model clicks, typing, downloads, screenshots, and page events for end-to-end checks.

use_cases.title: Scale Scraping Jobs
use_cases.description: Use page pools and isolated contexts to run controlled concurrent browser tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Rod Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single page workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use go-rod-master to plan a simple Rod browser task for a public page. Include navigation, waits, extraction goals, cleanup, and permission checks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Selectors to Rod Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an automation flow from page requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use go-rod-master to turn these page elements into a Rod workflow. Explain selectors, wait strategy, timeout handling, and error paths.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Concurrent Scraper
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate batch automation with resource limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use go-rod-master to design a concurrent scraping plan for these allowed URLs. Include page pool size, isolation, retries, rate limits, and result collection.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Rod Automation Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use go-rod-master to review this Rod automation design. Identify brittle waits, unsafe interception, missing cleanup, legal risks, and production hardening steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a Rod scraper for a public documentation page.
output: A short workflow covering browser launch, navigation, stable waits, content extraction, and cleanup.
Selector guidance for headings and links, with timeout handling for slow pages.
A note to verify permission, robots guidance, and request volume before running at scale.

output_examples.input: Improve a flaky Rod login test.
output: A diagnosis of missing waits, unstable click targets, and weak error handling.
Recommended use of explicit timeouts, stable element waits, and race selectors for success or error states.
Cleanup steps for browser contexts and downloaded artifacts.

output_examples.input: Review request interception in a browser automation flow.
output: A risk review covering header injection, response body changes, and safe test-only boundaries.
Recommendations to avoid real credentials in examples and restrict interception to owned systems.

best_practices: Use explicit timeouts, stable waits, and error-returning APIs for production automation.
Run scraping only on sites where you have permission and keep request volume controlled.
Close browsers, pages, contexts, and hijack routers with clear cleanup paths.
anti_patterns: Using stealth or proxy guidance to bypass access controls or site policies.
Injecting authorization headers or modifying responses on systems you do not own.
Starting unlimited browser instances or pages without memory and concurrency limits.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Go browser automation with Rod for rendered pages, tests, scraping workflows, and Chrome DevTools tasks.

faq.question: Does it run browser automation by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a developer can adapt into Go code.

faq.question: Is this safe for all scraping tasks?
faq.answer: No. You must confirm permission, follow site terms, and avoid bypassing controls or rate limits.

faq.question: Does it include stealth automation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The source includes stealth and anti-bot guidance, which creates dual-use risk.

faq.question: Can it help with testing owned applications?
faq.answer: Yes. Rod can automate browser flows, screenshots, downloads, and event checks for owned applications.

faq.question: What tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
